\[
V_\sigma = \begin{cases} \exp\!\left(-\frac{R_B^2}{2\beta^2}\right)\left(1 - \exp\!\left(-\frac{S^2}{2\gamma^2}\right)\right) & \text{if this is above } 0 \\ 1 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases},
\qquad
\beta = 0.5,\ \gamma = 15
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(\lambda_1, \lambda_2\): The Hessian eigenvalues, |lambda_1| <= |lambda_2|
- \(R_B\): The blob ratio
- \(S\): The structure, the norm of the Hessian
- \(\beta, \gamma\): The blob and structure constants

The hybrid Hessian filter of Ng and coworkers uses Frangi's vesselness with a fixed gamma. R_B = |lambda_1| / lambda_2 is the blob ratio and S the norm of the Hessian, as on the Frangi page. Where the curvature has the wrong sign for a ridge, scikit-image clips lambda_2, and the response becomes exactly 0. Then scikit-image sets every such pixel to 1, the largest value the measure can have. On the Disks image with dark ridges, this makes the inside of the disks white, while the dark background stays near 0. The result is stretched so the strongest response is white.
